synopsis: Across construction, mining and road studies, synthetic data supports training augmentation rather than substitution: mixed real-and-synthetic training generally performs better in data-poor settings, while synthetic-only training leaves a domain gap [f7047, f12900]. A 2023 construction-worker study, reported through a secondary summary, reduced real-image needs by 50% and improved detector performance by 16%; a 2025 construction-object study achieved its best result with 1,500 real plus 1,500 synthetic images [f7049, f7050, f7051]. Benefits are context-dependent: on-road synthetic-fog pre-training followed by real-fog fine-tuning added at most 0.0117 mAP, and broader synthetic coverage can inflate mAP despite domain differences [f4896, f4818]. Generative models can create new views, rare scenarios and weather variations, but whether weather editing preserves sensor physics remains uncertain, and hybrid models’ maturity for safety credit is unresolved [f3819, f3824, f4308, f5078]. Reported reality gaps include rendered excavators and Unity construction scenes, although the cited 2025 review and 2026 Unity study are preprints; no peer-reviewed demonstration was found that synthetic-only training or validation establishes heavy off-road collision-avoidance reliability [f10582, f10584, f10585, f6690]. Planning should therefore use generated data to target training gaps, test detectors on untouched real data, and document validation-data independence; validation and estimation data must be real or physically independent of the training-data generator [f12890, f12885].
